item.title: Kerama Islands Guide: Ferries, Snorkelling & Beaches
item.description: A short ferry ride west of Naha, the Kerama Islands are a national park famed for some of the clearest, most luminous water in Japan — a turquoise so distinctive it has its own name, “Kerama Blue.” With brilliant coral reefs, sea turtles, and powder-white beaches, the islands (chiefly Zamami, Aka and Tokashiki) are a snorkelling and diving paradise, doable as a day trip or an overnight escape. They’re also a winter whale-watching spot.

item.title: Okinawa Diving & Snorkelling Guide: Spots, Trips & Tips
item.description: With warm, gin-clear seas, vast coral reefs and abundant marine life, Okinawa is one of Asia’s great diving and snorkelling destinations. From the dazzling “Kerama Blue” reefs and the glowing Blue Cave off Cape Maeda, to manta cleaning stations and the mysterious Yonaguni Monument, there’s something for every level — including easy trial (“experience”) dives for total beginners and snorkelling trips for non-divers. Operators across the island make it simple to get in the water.

item.title: Kerama Islands & Okinawa Coral Reefs: The Complete Guide
item.description: The Kerama Islands — 30 km west of Naha — contain some of the most pristine coral reefs in East Asia. Marine biologists have recorded over 250 species of coral and 360 species of fish in the Kerama Shoto National Park. The water clarity here — what the Japanese call “Kerama Blue” (ケラマブルー) — is the result of both the Kuroshio Current and the absence of agricultural runoff on these small uninhabited or lightly populated islands.
